question.text: An object travels along a straight line such that its x-coordinate varies with time according to the equation x = (2 + t² + 2t³), where x is expressed in metres and time t is in seconds. Determine:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: the location from which the object began its motion,

parts.label: b
parts.asks: the initial velocity of the object,

parts.label: c
parts.asks: the acceleration of the object at t = 2 s.

solution.approach: Read the starting position directly from x at t = 0, then differentiate x once and twice for velocity and acceleration.

steps.text: The particle's starting position is x at t = 0.
Differentiate x with respect to time to get the velocity, then substitute t = 0.
Differentiate v with respect to time to get the acceleration, then substitute t = 2 s.

common_mistakes.text: Reporting the velocity at t = 2 s, which is 28 m/s, instead of differentiating a second time for the acceleration, which is 26 m/s².
